title: Vardy 2015-16 v Shearer 1994-95: the greatest title-winning striker season?
sources: data/competition-history/premier-league.json (champions, runners-up, top scorers, FWA winners 1992-93 to 2025-26)
checked: Vardy 24 league goals, 11 games in a row breaking Van Nistelrooy's record, Leicester 81 points, 5000-1 pre-season odds, Mahrez PFA (Wikipedia season page); Vardy FWA award and Leicester champions with Arsenal second (local file). Shearer 34 league / 37 all comps, Golden Boot, PFA, Blackburn 89 points one ahead of United, 2-1 final-day defeat at Anfield with Shearer scoring while United drew at West Ham (Wikipedia season page); 34 goals and the title (local file). 'Each club's only Premier League title' checked against the full champions list in the local file.

lines.text: Two strikers. Two clubs that have won the Premier League exactly once. Whose title season was better?
Alan Shearer, nineteen ninety-four, ninety-five. Blackburn Rovers.
Thirty-four league goals. Thirty-seven in all competitions. Players' Player of the Year.
Jamie Vardy, twenty fifteen, sixteen. Leicester City. Five thousand to one.
Twenty-four league goals, and a goal in eleven games in a row. A Premier League record.
On goals alone, Shearer wins easily. Ten more.
But Shearer's season had forty-two games. Vardy's had thirty-eight.
Trophies? Same answer. Both won the league.
Now the twist. It's still the only Premier League title either club has ever won.

scene.heading: THE TWIST
scene.body: Blackburn 1995. Leicester 2016. Neither club has won the Premier League before or since.

lines.text: Blackburn nearly blew it. They lost on the final day at Anfield, and won the title by one point.
Shearer scored that day too, of course.
Leicester started the season at five thousand to one, and won it with eighty-one points.
Shearer had the better numbers. Vardy had the bigger miracle. For the best season, Shearer. For the best story, Vardy.
